summary: The finite bounded native source-v1 TaskRun contract, server authority, authenticated HTTP replay, process-loss boundaries, packaging and regressions satisfy ADR-0035 on the reviewed source bytes. This closes N1.4 only; whole-worker reconstruction, online GC, production HA and throughput remain outside the claim.

combined_source_http_process_package_con.qualification: Exploratory predecessor. The final authoritative rerun is final_source_bound_profiles.native_http on the frozen source manifest.

guarantees: A PostgreSQL trigger held the source-record INSERT transaction on an observed ungranted advisory lock; SIGKILL of the API before commit left accepted position, record count and prefix unchanged.

A child client committed append position 1 and then called os._exit(77); after API restart, normal Failed-to-AwaitingRetry-to-Running orchestration advanced the same TaskRun to attempt 2, a fresh source owner resumed at position 2, and the old binding could not mutate progress.
After durable EOF and API restart, exact admission returned COMPLETED at the durable position and exact close replay remained idempotent.
source_process_loss.identity_scope: The caller retained exact FlowRun, TaskRun, stream, owner and position identities. This is low-level intent replay plus ordinary TaskRun retry, not whole-worker reconstruction.

checks: config-only serialization without live clients or credentials
permanent capacity refusal is not retried
terminal and source append intents freeze before transport
multiple source publications reuse the owning client context

static_and_surface_checks.ui_build_status: PASS; sequential build completed in 4.83 seconds

acceptance_criteria_review.finding: Real sync and async source generators execute as ordinary Prefect TaskRuns through authenticated HTTP and PostgreSQL 17.

SourceContext is informational; the engine initializes and advances a separate local counter only from durable admission and append acceptance, so user mutation of the context cannot advance platform progress.
Multiple records from one generator attempt, early downstream delivery before source completion, and exact EOF were observed in both sync and async profiles.
Before-acceptance failure redelivers document 200; commit-before-response retry resumes with 201.
Exact append and EOF replay, content drift refusal, owner replacement and stale-attempt refusal preserve the durable position.
Pre-owner startup failures reject exact reservations, intermediate retry keeps the source OPEN, and final TaskRun lifecycle failure is separately authorized.
The scale control retains one TaskRun and stream while record count grows; no orchestration state/event is created per source record.
EOF zero, gaps, wrong event types, non-JSON values, non-None returns, unsupported runners and unbounded declarations fail in their declared safe phase.

Final legacy, kernel, client, PostgreSQL migration, SQLite capability and store/API profiles passed on the same source manifest; client packaging and ordinary operator/source regressions are included.
Real PG17/HTTP process-loss boundaries cover precommit API death, accepted append plus client death, owner takeover, API restart and EOF replay on the reviewed test source hash.
This review explicitly limits recovery evidence to TaskRun retry and retained low-level identities; whole-worker submission reconstruction remains deferred.

retained_negative_findings.finding: The first real SDK profile found that parameter resolution assumed every stream config had an input. The accepted fix limits stream dependency allowance to StreamTaskConfig; source parameters follow ordinary finite resolution.

The first precommit fault test used the SDK client's built-in transport retry, which prevented a bounded caller observation after API death. The successor uses a raw authenticated nonretrying request against the same production API and retains the failed trial.

The first stale-owner assertion expected STALE_OWNER, while the documented current-TaskRun authority check correctly returned ATTEMPT_NOT_CURRENT first. The successor asserts that exact precedence and verifies no position mutation.

An initial UI build overlapped npm dependency installation and failed with missing TypeScript/node_modules files. It is not acceptance evidence. After hooks and installation completed, the sequential build in native-stage4-ui-build-final-2026-11-02.log passed.

nonblocking_limitations: A user generator close or aclose exception can replace an earlier exception's diagnostic. It remains on a failure path and cannot accept a record or successful EOF, but diagnostic preservation may be improved later.
The accepted profile is finite, contiguous, JSON-only and bounded by frozen capacity.
The Python generator frame, flow future graph and whole-worker submission are not reconstructed.
Online prefix reclamation, indefinite sources, managed ObjectRef services, external connector transactions, generalized fan-out, production HA and throughput acceptance are outside N1.4.
The tiny in-process generator probe in ADR-0035 is design evidence only and is excluded from acceptance counts.

The final parallel kernel profile emitted the previously observed multiprocessing resource_tracker KeyError diagnostics while completing 718 passes and 2 known xfails; the accepted runtime assertions did not fail.

verdict_history.reason: The final kernel, legacy, storage, PostgreSQL migration, SQLite capability and client regression profiles were still running.

All seven final source-bound profiles passed on an identical source manifest with zero drift; the sequential UI build also passed and the earlier parallel build race remains disclosed as negative evidence.
